_comment: nina-review-role.json - a DENY-BY-DEFAULT skeleton for the IAM role nina's live-read
mode runs as. This is NOT a live policy and this repo ships no account: the operator
adapts it. Its job is that the adaptation starts from deny-by-default rather than from
the managed ReadOnlyAccess policy, which reaches data actions and auto-extends to new
services on the provider's schedule.
APPLY: extract the policy document, which is the value of .PolicyDocument -
jq '.PolicyDocument' tests/policy/nina-review-role.json > nina-review-role-policy.json
The wrapper exists because JSON has no comments and IAM rejects unknown top-level keys.
WHY IT WORKS AT ALL: an explicit Deny beats any Allow in the IAM evaluation chain.
That is the one evaluation-chain fact this design leans on, and the operator can add
Allow statements for the read families they intend to grant without weakening these.
SCOPE (D15): live reads are AWS-ONLY. This file is an AWS IAM policy and denies
NOTHING on Azure or GCP, where two of the three known projection bypasses lived
(az keyvault secret show, az storage account keys list). Until Azure custom-role
notActions and GCP deny-policy siblings exist and are tested, nina runs docs-plus-IaC
only on those providers. Bucket members that are az/gcloud verbs are therefore absent
from this file by design, not by oversight.
compute.projects.get is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It is a GCP permission and cannot sit in
an AWS IAM Statement; an earlier draft listed it here, which would have shipped a
policy that fails to parse or silently ignores the entry. The fifth defeating call
(gcloud compute project-info describe) is out of live-read scope under D15 and stays
denied by condition 2 in agents/nina.md.
=== WHAT IAM CANNOT SEE - read this before mistaking a shipped policy for a closed
surface. This file is DEFENCE IN DEPTH BEHIND condition 2 of agents/nina.md, never a
substitute for it. Coverage is PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION: ===
1. IAM cannot see a projection. 'aws ec2 describe-instance-attribute --attribute
userData' and 'aws apigateway get-api-keys --include-values' are denied in nina's
persona text as whole calls, but IAM sees only ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and
apigateway:GET - denying either outright removes every attribute and every API
read, including the benign ones her review needs.
2. The same limit applies to every Bucket-2 projection-only member: the difference
between a permitted and a denied call is the --query/--format expression, which
never reaches the IAM evaluation.
3. Client-side credential minting has no IAM action to deny. 'aws eks get-token' and
'aws s3 presign' sign locally from credentials the principal already holds; no
API call is made, so no Deny can fire. Same for 'aws rds generate-db-auth-token' -
rds-db:connect below denies the USE of such a token, not its generation.
4. Bucket 5 is entirely outside IAM. Reading ~/.aws/credentials, env, terraform state,
git history, or the IMDS endpoint at 169.254.169.254 needs no provider grant at
all. The only control there is nina's persona text and the harness's tool grants.
=== THE C1 STATEMENT COSTS REVIEW CAPABILITY - decide deliberately ===
DenyDefeatingCallsC1 denies four calls that defeated an earlier, verb-only version of
the allowlist. Three of them (cloudformation:DescribeStacks, ecs:DescribeTasks,
lambda:ListFunctions) are calls nina legitimately needs to review stack, task and
function configuration - denying them outright costs real review capability. They are
in their own statement so the operator can drop it KNOWINGLY, accepting that condition
2b's response-shape rule becomes the only thing standing behind those three.
